clue.text: Having lost capital cover, to be blunt

definitions.meaning: capital is the head, and its cover is hair, so this describes someone hairless on top
a blunt, unadorned statement is called a plain or stark one

explanation.surface: Someone told to speak frankly about having lost their hat.
explanation.definitionFit: Hairless on the head is one sense; plain and unvarnished, as in a statement, is the other.

clue.text: A purchaser we're told of, for the farm building

indicators.note: what we are told is heard rather than read, so the word is taken by its sound

parts.note: a purchaser is a buyer

explanation.surface: A remark about who bought the cowshed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'we're told' signals that the word for a purchaser is said aloud, giving a word with the same sound but different spelling.
explanation.definitionFit: A cowshed is the classic farm building of this name.

clue.text: Fruit for Harry

definitions.meaning: Harry ... is the racketeer in the film The Third Man

explanation.surface: Picking a piece of fruit for someone called Harry.
explanation.definitionFit: A green citrus fruit; and the surname of Harry, the villain of the film The Third Man.

clue.text: Thrashed around, having failed to get in first lifeboat

indicators.note: one piece is told to get in, so it goes inside the other word
first means only the opening letter of lifeboat is used

explanation.surface: Someone thrashing about in the water after failing to board the lifeboat first.
explanation.walkthrough: 'first' takes L from lifeboat; 'to get in' puts it inside FAILED, after the F.
explanation.definitionFit: Thrashing around is wildly swinging the arms or limbs about.

clue.text: Were these punk rockers thugs?

parts.note: names a British punk band of the 1970s whose name suggests violent men who choke their victims

explanation.surface: A question whether a punk group were really violent.
explanation.definitionFit: The Stranglers were a leading British punk rock band; a stranglers is also a thug who throttles people.

clue.text: Are his girlfriends always late?

parts.note: late means dead, not tardy: a man whose women end up dead is a womaniser by another name

explanation.surface: A complaint about a man whose dates never arrive on time.
explanation.definitionFit: A womanising charmer, literally read as a man who kills women, so his girlfriends are the late ones.

clue.text: Holds back the others after monsoon season

parts.note: the rest means the others, the remainder
the monsoon season is known as the rains in India

explanation.surface: Someone keeping the others back until the monsoon is over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after' is a loose link here, not a placement signal: the pieces sit in the order the clue gives them. In India the monsoon season is simply called the rains.
explanation.definitionFit: To hold back is to keep in check or curb.

clue.text: English repeats of die fledermaus? That's crazy!

definitions.meaning: Die Fledermaus is German for the bat, so several of them in English
mad, as in having ... in the belfry

explanation.surface: Someone dismissing an English remake of the Strauss operetta as mad.
explanation.definitionFit: Winged night mammals, the English for Fledermaus, and slang for mad or eccentric.

clue.text: Able to get no bed for treatment to scapula

indicators.note: treatment of the letters works them into a fresh arrangement

explanation.surface: A patient able to manage without a hospital bed for shoulder treatment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for treatment' signals that ABLE and NO BED are mixed up together.
explanation.definitionFit: The shoulder blade is the everyday name for the scapula.

clue.text: Study of consumption cites tide movements

indicators.note: movements of the letters shift them into a new order

explanation.surface: A study citing tides in connection with eating habits.
explanation.walkthrough: 'movements' signals that CITES TIDE is rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: The science of diet and nutrition studies what people eat.

clue.text: Sesame seed found inside stillroom

indicators.note: the letters are found inside the word stillroom

explanation.surface: Sesame seeds stored in a household pantry.
explanation.walkthrough: A stillroom is a pantry or distilling room in a large house.
explanation.definitionFit: The Indian name for sesame, the plant and its seed.

clue.text: His access to the garden was cut off by a barrier

definitions.text: His access to the garden was cut off

parts.note: a dam is a barrier across water

explanation.surface: A man shut out of the garden by a barrier.
explanation.walkthrough: The garden is Eden, from which the first man was expelled.
explanation.definitionFit: The first man in Genesis was barred from Eden after the Fall.

clue.text: What you call a fox today

definitions.text: What you call a fox today

parts.words: What you call a fox today
parts.note: asks for a dialect name for a fox, its letters also opening the word today

explanation.surface: A question about the modern word for a fox.
explanation.definitionFit: A Scottish and northern English dialect word for a fox, found also at the start of today.

clue.text: It's not much for a drink

explanation.surface: A modest remark that an order is very little for a drink.
explanation.definitionFit: Weak, cheap beer, and by extension anything trivial or of little account.

clue.text: A salvo or an explosion caused by rebellious Italian monk

indicators.note: an explosion blows the letters apart into a new order

explanation.surface: A rebellious friar provoking a salvo of gunfire.
explanation.walkthrough: 'explosion' signals that A SALVO OR AN is rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Girolamo Savonarola was the Dominican friar who defied the Pope in fifteenth-century Florence.

clue.text: A gay plant design for the wallcovering

indicators.note: a design arranges the letters into a fresh pattern

explanation.surface: A cheerful floral pattern for wallpaper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'design' signals that A GAY PLANT is rearranged. Anaglypta is a British brand of embossed wallpaper.
explanation.definitionFit: A trade name for a thick, embossed wallpaper meant to be painted over.

clue.text: Observing game when court card is playing

parts.note: loo is an old card game
the king is a court card
on means playing, as an actor on stage

explanation.surface: Watching a card game while a king is in play.
explanation.walkthrough: Loo is an old card game played for stakes.
explanation.definitionFit: Watching as a spectator without taking part.

clue.text: They're laid, for example, at both ends of gardens

parts.note: eg abbreviates exempli gratia, for example

indicators.note: both ends means the first and last letters of gardens

explanation.surface: Something laid in a garden, at both ends.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at both ends of' takes G and S, the first and last letters of gardens.
explanation.definitionFit: Hens and other birds lay these shelled ova.

clue.text: Flier offering a way to the hill

parts.note: via is Latin for way, as in a route
a tor is a rocky hill, as on Dartmoor

explanation.surface: Someone offering a route up the hill.
explanation.walkthrough: A tor is a rocky hilltop, found on Dartmoor in south-west England.
explanation.definitionFit: A pilot of an aircraft, one who flies.

clue.text: What 17 did to confuse polite little daughter

indicators.note: to confuse the letters is to jumble them up

parts.note: d is the short form of daughter

explanation.surface: A pilot set out to confuse a well-mannered small girl.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to confuse' signals that POLITE is rearranged; 17 is the flier, so his action is to fly the plane.
explanation.definitionFit: A flier steered or flew the aircraft.

clue.text: A poet with money to burn?

definitions.text: A poet with money to burn?

parts.words: A poet with money to burn?
parts.note: names an English poet whose surname describes someone who is lavish with cash

explanation.surface: A question about a wealthy poet.
explanation.definitionFit: Stephen Spender was an English poet; a big spender splashes money around.

clue.text: A zero given to this dyestuff

parts.note: nil means zero

explanation.surface: A dye being awarded no marks.
explanation.definitionFit: Indigo dye, or the shrub it is made from.

clue.text: I'm taking advertisements — they're not what they seem

parts.note: posters are printed advertisements

explanation.surface: Someone complaining that adverts are deceptive.
explanation.definitionFit: Frauds and pretenders pass themselves off as someone else.

clue.text: It may be a bind, having to wear one

definitions.text: It may be a bind, having to wear one

parts.words: It may be a bind, having to wear one
parts.note: a tedious obligation, here an item round the neck, or a fastening that binds

explanation.surface: Someone grumbling about a dress code requiring neckwear.
explanation.definitionFit: A necktie is a chore to wear, and to fasten is to bind.

clue.text: A wistful urge for a note from Japan?

definitions.meaning: the Japanese currency, issued in banknotes

explanation.surface: A longing to receive a letter from Japan.
explanation.definitionFit: A longing; and the Japanese currency, here as a banknote.

clue.text: Hold onto one's overnight bag

definitions.meaning: a dated word for a travelling bag or holdall

explanation.surface: Someone clinging to their weekend bag.
explanation.definitionFit: To grasp tightly; and an old American word for a small travelling bag.

clue.text: Well-bred softies?

parts.note: split into two words, mild males; as one, men of good breeding

explanation.surface: A question about whether the upper classes are soft.
explanation.definitionFit: Refined, courteous men; read in two parts, mild males.

clue.text: Told to stay down on the mattress

indicators.note: something told is spoken, so the phrase is taken by its sound

parts.note: to lie low is to stay down out of sight

explanation.surface: Someone being told to keep down on an airbed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Told' signals a sound-alike of the phrase meaning to stay down out of sight. A Lilo is a British brand of inflatable airbed.
explanation.definitionFit: An inflatable airbed used on the beach or for camping.

clue.text: Came out with a spice from the east Indies

indicators.note: out signals the letters are put out of their usual order

explanation.surface: Someone returning with a spice from the East Indies.
explanation.definitionFit: The spice made from the dried husk around the nutmeg seed.

clue.text: Pry, and no quarter is given!

parts.note: a quarter is a compass point, here south-east

explanation.surface: A cry that no mercy will be shown.
explanation.walkthrough: Compass points are called quarters, so SE stands for one of them.
explanation.definitionFit: To poke about in others' business, as in being nosy.

clue.text: Seaweed found in two southern states

parts.note: AL is the postal code for Alabama
GA is the postal code for Georgia

explanation.surface: Seaweed growing in two states of the American South.
explanation.walkthrough: Alabama (AL) and Georgia (GA) are both southern US states.
explanation.definitionFit: A simple water plant, the singular of the group that includes kelp and wrack.

clue.text: There must be a point to such a container

definitions.text: There must be a point to such a container

parts.words: There must be a point to such a container
parts.note: a box whose contents are sharp sewing implements, each with a point

explanation.surface: A philosophical remark that a box must have a purpose.
explanation.definitionFit: A small holder for sewing pins and similar sharp tools.
